name: Lodha Developers Ltd
title: Lodha Developers Ltd - 543287 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 PAT INR 13.7bn (more than double, 26.9% margin) helped by ~INR 6bn land sale PAT; pre-sales flat-ish at INR 46.3bn with launches deliberately deferred, FY27 PAT guide ~INR 41bn reaffirmed.

triggers.label: FY27 PAT guide ~INR 41bn reaffirmed

triggers.label: Price growth 5-7% planned
triggers.quote: In the near term, we expect to enhance our pricing by 5% to 7% across different micro markets over the year.

triggers.quote: Pre-sales for the quarter were INR 46.3 billion, up 4% year-on-year.

summary.headline: Lodha Q1 FY27 PAT more than doubled to INR 13.7 billion (26.9% margin) on land sales, while pre-sales rose only 4% to INR 46.3 billion.
summary.overview: Revenue rose 43% YoY to INR 50 billion and adjusted EBITDA rose 79% to INR 21.5 billion at a 43% margin, with PAT of INR 13.7 billion versus INR 6.8 billion a year ago. Management said the quarter was flattered by roughly half of the year's planned land sales, including data centre park land sold to Digital Edge India at about INR 420 million per acre. Residential pre-sales were deliberately weak because about one-third of normal launches were postponed to Q2 on Middle East conflict concerns. Net debt fell by INR 4.5 billion to under INR 50 billion, with net debt to equity at about 0.2x.

segments.name: Residential (DevCo)
segments.commentary: Pre-sales of INR 46.3 billion with only one Mumbai launch (about 0.4 million sq ft); sustenance sales drove the quarter. Premium and luxury made up almost 60% of sales, and mid-income (below INR 3 crore) about 50% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Land sales
segments.commentary: Data centre and other land pre-sales of about INR 12 billion, with PAT contribution of about INR 6 billion. Management guides land sales of INR 20-30 billion a year for the next several years.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo
segments.commentary: June exit run-rate of about INR 3 billion with no data centre contribution. Target is over INR 30 billion by FY32, including about INR 20 billion-plus from data centres, INR 6 billion from retail and office, and INR 4 billion from warehousing and industrial.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT guidance of about 20% growth on INR 34.3 billion, i.e. about INR 41 billion; Q1 delivered 33% of this. Management said 20% is an annual target and warned against annualising the quarter.
FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 240 billion reaffirmed, with H1 at 40-42% of the full year. Q2 pre-sales expected at INR 50 billion or more, with July off to a good start.
Embedded margin excluding land sales was in the early 30s; full-year margin guidance of 32-34% retained, with no expectation of margins in the 40s.
Medium-term PAT growth of about 20% a year, taking PAT beyond INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE expected to move toward 20% from about 16% in FY26 but may not reach it.
DevCo to be net debt-free within 2-3 years; net debt to equity to stay below the 0.5x ceiling.
Pricing to rise 5-7% across micro markets over the year, with room for a further 100-200 bps.
Dividend policy of 15-20% of PAT, then debt reduction, then buyback or special dividend.
capex_capacity: Data centre park: about 660 acres at Palava, with about 3 GW of power tie-up, 5 fibre routes and 5 transmission lines. About 130 acres of the first 370-acre phase is sold; about 150 more acres are to be sold over 3-4 years at about INR 600 million per acre (about INR 90 billion).

Plan to build about 1 GW of powered shell on about 90 acres, generating over INR 20 billion of annual rent by FY32. Leasing of the first box is targeted within FY27, with physical work on the company's own box to start in calendar 2026.
Estimated capex for the power-shell infrastructure is INR 500-700 crore over time, per the CFO-level answer on infrastructure.
Power density is 11-15 MW per acre. Management does not yet plan chips or racks and sees turnkey shell at least two years away.
demand_pricing: Middle East NRI buyers are about 4-5% of sales. Management sees the impact as moderate and expects NRI and US-based buyers to shift some money toward Indian homes.
Construction cost: if energy-linked inflation persists for a full year, management expects a 1-1.5% rise in project cost (35-75 bps project EBITDA impact). Supply chain is about 95% domestic.
Conversion rate reportedly 8% or higher from July, with a long-run aim of 10%.
Sales from new cities (Pune, Bangalore, NCR, MMR) to reach 30-45% of pre-sales in the medium term.

Palava land sale price rose to about INR 420 million per acre from about INR 210 million in calendar 2025. Management puts fair market value at about INR 650 million per acre, reachable in about 18 months.
Competition described as rational. Branded share of MMR is about 30%, which management expects to reach 40-45% by the end of the decade.

qa_highlights.question: What was the value and margin of the land sales in the quarter, and how much did they add to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore of land pre-sales including data centre land, with revenue recognised at 85-90% of that. PAT contribution was about INR 600 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the data centre rental estimate appear to fall from INR 30 billion to INR 20 billion-plus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change. The INR 30 billion FY32 target is unchanged, and data centres account for INR 20 billion-plus of it. Powered shell rent is a little over INR 20 million per MW a year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the pre-sales guidance factor in the Middle East war, and is there upside if it ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been contained and the guidance is maintained. It will review once the conflict ends. MMR high-value sales have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any margin outlook beyond the guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Embedded margins excluding land were in the early 30s. Management said the 40s-level margin was driven by forward-loaded land sales and that the full-year guidance of early 30s stands.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed per acre for a data centre land sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost is about 10-15% of the sales price, and the CFO put group infrastructure capex at INR 500-700 crore over time. Most of the sale price flows through to cash after tax.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company compete with its data centre buyers, and what is its competitive edge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company offers powered shell, which no other provider offers, and that its advantages are land, power, recycled water, ecosystem and relationships.

risks_watch: Pre-sales were up only 4% YoY; the FY27 target of INR 240 billion requires H2 weighting, with about INR 250 billion of GDV in the launch calendar.
Land sales are lumpy and drove a large share of PAT; the 20% PAT growth target is annual, so quarterly results will vary.
Middle East conflict is prolonged. Energy-linked construction cost inflation could reach 1-1.5% if it lasts a full year.
Data centre economics depend on signed leases, which are not yet in place. Power beyond the 3 GW tie-up is still under work, and the first lease is expected within FY27.
Connectivity openings (Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway, Upper Thane connector) are expected after the monsoon. Impact on Palava sales is expected from Q4 and meaningful mainly in FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, cash and the data centre thesis, but deliberately cautious on near-term residential demand. Management openly explained the low pre-sales as a launch-timing decision and called the geopolitical outlook uncertain. It repeatedly warned against annualising the quarter.
key_quotes: Our commitment of 20% PAT growth is an annual guidance, not a quarterly one.
Funding all of our growth from operations while simultaneously deleveraging is, in my view, the genuine signal in this quarter, more so than any other number.
This was a decision, not an outcome.
The data center build is largely self-funded from land sales inside the same park. It does not add to group leverage, and it does not compete with our DevCo for capital in any significant manner.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About one-third of normal residential launches were postponed from Q1 into Q2, and INR 250 billion of GDV sits in the launch calendar against the INR 240 billion pre-sales target.

rows.why: About 130 acres of the 370-acre phase already sold, with 150 more acres to sell over 3-4 years at about INR 600 million per acre (about INR 90 billion), and Palava land price up to INR 420 million per acre from INR 210 million in calendar 2025.

rows.label: Net debt reduction to net-debt-free DevCo
rows.why: Net debt fell INR 4.5 billion in the quarter to under INR 50 billion, net debt to equity about 0.2x against a 0.5x ceiling, and management intends to be effectively debt-free in 2-3 years.

rows.label: Price increases of 5-7% across micro markets
rows.why: Management plans 5-7% pricing rise over the year with room for a further 100-200 bps, and Palava land price rose about 100% (INR 210 million to INR 420 million per acre) in the past year.
